@@ -0,0 +1,147 @@ +### Design proposal for a job worker service +rafael.vanoni@pm.me
+5/3/2025 + +#### Objectives + +As stated in the challenge description [[1]](#1), the goal of this project is to prototype a job worker service that provides an API to start, stop, query the status and stream the output of arbitrary Linux processes. This functionality will be implemented through a library and wrapped by an API server, along with a command line interface that communicates with the server. + +#### Scope + +This project will follow a "shrink to fit" approach, aiming to implement only the core components needed to provide a job service and nothing more. It will deliver a library, an API server, a client program and tests to verify the functionality. + +There are components of each of these deliverables that fall outside of our immediate scope, such as certificate generation, service monitoring, high availability, user management and secure logging. These are considered out of scope and will not be implemented in this project. We will also not deliver any documentation outside of this design document. + +#### Implementation Plan + +This project will be implemented in Go, using the native modules [[2]](#2) support for dependency management with 64 bit Linux as the target architecture. We'll use gRPC [[3]](#3) to implement our service APIs. + +User authentication will be implemented with mTLS [[4]](#4) and gRPC interceptors [[5]](#5) that verify user credentials against a simple, hard coded table of test users. This table will also indicate a set of privileges and permissions for each user. User accounting will be accomplished through server logging. + +Job execution will be managed by the server through Go routines. They will be allowed to execute while the server is running, but will be stopped (along with any child processes) if the server is stopped, if the user issues a 'stop' command or if any underlying processes terminate unexpectedly. The user must query the status of a job to learn of any such condition(s) (as there'll be no notification mechanism) or be streaming the job output at the time of termination. + +Output streaming will use gRPC server-side streams. Jobs will be executed under the calling user's own credentials, requiring them to have been created and configured ahead of time. + +Server log messages will be written to files in the server's host environment. These will be separated according to different functional areas, such as user accounting, server execution logs, job execution, etc. + +Resource control will be implemented through job priorities set by the user upon job creation. These will be a simple [1..5] range, with more resources being given to higher priority jobs [[6]](#6). If the user does not specify a priority, the lowest priority will be utilized. On the server side, we'll use control groups [[7]](#7) to enforce resource allocation. + +#### Proposed API + +Our worker library will be centered around a job service, with methods to start, stop, query status and stream the output of a job. We'll include a simple login method for user authntication. Here are the proposed methods: + +|Method|Arguments|Response| +|---|---|---| +|start|linux executable with arguments
optional priority value [1..5]|Success: job ID
Failure: error message| +|stop|Job ID|Success: job summary
Failure: error message| +|status|Job ID|Success: job summary
Failure: error message| +|stream|Job ID|Success: job output
Failure: error message| +|login|User name and password|Success: auth token
Failure: error message| + +And the current .proto file: + +``` +syntax = "proto3"; + +option go_package = "./jobservice"; + +package jobservice; + +service JobService { + rpc Start(Spec) returns (Id) {} + rpc Stop(Id) returns (Summary) {} + rpc Status(Id) returns (Summary) {} + rpc Stream(Id) returns (stream Output) {} +} + +message Spec { + string user = 1; + string token = 2; + string command = 3; + int32 priority = 4; +} + +message Id { + string id = 1; +} + +message Summary { + string status = 1; + string message = 2; +} + +message Output { + string message = 1; +} + +service LoginService { + rpc Login(Credentials) returns (LoginResponse) {} +} + +message Credentials { + string user = 1; + string password = 2; +} + +message LoginResponse { + string token = 1; +} +``` + +#### Client UX + +Here are some examples of the proposed client interface and the expected responses: + +###### User authentication +``` +[06:20:10] $ client login -p correctPassword userOne +Login successful +``` +###### Starting a job +``` +[06:20:15] $ client start while true; do date; sleep 1; done +Starting job 33673d54-294f-11f0-87b4-e3e701882dc4 +Sun May 4 06:20:16 PM PDT 2025 +Sun May 4 06:20:17 PM PDT 2025 +[...] +``` +###### Stopping a job +``` +[06:20:20] $ client stop 33673d54-294f-11f0-87b4-e3e701882dc4 +Job 33673d54-294f-11f0-87b4-e3e701882dc4 stopped after 5 seconds +``` +###### Querying the status of a job +``` +[06:20:17] $ client status 33673d54-294f-11f0-87b4-e3e701882dc4 +Job 33673d54-294f-11f0-87b4-e3e701882dc4 has been running for 2 seconds +``` +###### Streaming the output of a job +``` +[06:20:18] $ client stream 33673d54-294f-11f0-87b4-e3e701882dc4 +Sun May 4 06:20:16 PM PDT 2025 +Sun May 4 06:20:17 PM PDT 2025 +Sun May 4 06:20:18 PM PDT 2025 +[...] +``` + +#### Security Considerations + +As mentioned earlier, we'll use mTLS as the authentication method for our service. We'll limit our implementation to TLS v1.3 ciphers for simplicity, and use a simple static user table for authorization. + +The main security challenge in this project is the fact that we'll be allowing the execution of arbitrary Linux processes by a remote client in a non virtualized context. We can attempt to mitigate the security risks by executing jobs with restricted user accounts, which unfortunately still leaves us with some serious concerns (unpatched CVEs, resource abuse attacks, etc). + +In a real world scenario, we would implement a proper user database with password hashing and salting. Server logs would be stored securely and in redundant locations. Job execution would occur in a virtual environment, with virtualized hardware resources.
